answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every identity to post a refundable stake peers can slash on proven misbehavior — like a harbor master charging each ship at the wharf a deposit before it docks. One bad actor pays one deposit; a thousand fakes must pay a thousand. Add slow-earned reputation: an orchard takes seasons to bear fruit, so a new identity has no standing until it completes verified useful work. Sybil farms then hit a ledge they cannot climb cheaply — each fake must earn trust one honest transaction at a time, making scale itself the cost.
